messages:
Ava (PM): Quick sync — we've had a couple support tickets about saved-query results showing different cost previews depending on which model variant is selected. want to avoid surprises when users pin per-route filters + per-model presets.
Diego (FE): Saw that. Repro steps? I tried with a route that has a canary model and main model; the cost preview flips when you change the model dropdown.
Priya (BE): Repro: user scopes a saved view to route:/nlp/embedding, adds filter user_country=US, pins model=fast-quant. Backend resolves route->model via routing policy and then merges cost estimates from cost-service. There may be a race where the UI asks for cost for a model that the routing policy will later override.
Sam (Telemetry): Logged an example: trace id 0x7ab3 — UI requested cost for model_id=fast-quant at t0, routing did a fallback to fast-quant-v2 at t0+120ms. Users saw prefetch cost for v1 then result tokens came from v2.
Nina (Design): UX ask: can we surface "model pinned" vs "routing-assigned" distinction? Maybe a small badge "pinned" and an info tooltip: "Routing can still replace model if capacity constraints apply."
Ava (PM): Two product questions: 1) Should saved views persist the pinned model choice or the routing policy selector? 2) Do we notify users when a saved view resolves to a different served model at runtime (quota fallback)?
Diego (FE): Implementation-wise we could show both: primary label shows pinned model, subtext shows effective model. Quick mock:
```
Pinned: fast-quant  •  Effective: fast-quant-v2 (fallback due to capacity)
```
Priya (BE): Backend needs to return both the requested_model (optional) and effective_model in the saved-view preview API. Current schema only returns effective_model. Changing that is a small API bump but consumers will need to handle the new field.
Sam (Telemetry): Also add telemetry events: saved_view.preview.requested_model, saved_view.preview.effective_model, and saved_view.preview.fallback_reason (values: quota, region, routing_policy). That'll let us alert on frequent surprises.
Ava (PM): Good. Also related — quota notifications. Some customers expect a warning when a saved query will exceed their per-route quota if run at scale. We should surface that on save.
Priya (BE): We can call quota-service during save/preview. But note: estimate depends on sampling assumptions (batch size, prefix cache hit). We'll return an estimate bucket like low/med/high and a numeric expected tokens.
Nina (Design): UI suggestion: show a colored pill next to the save button: green (OK), amber (might exceed), red (likely exceed). Hover shows assumptions and how we estimated (e.g., 90th pct traffic).
Diego (FE): Frontend changes: 1) saved-view preview panel must show requested vs effective model; 2) cost/tokens estimate + quota pill; 3) small CTA: "Re-evaluate with routing policy X" to let customers preview results under different policies.
Priya (BE): API sketch for saved view preview:
```
GET /api/v1/saved_views/:id/preview?route=/nlp/embedding
Response: {
  "requested_model": "fast-quant",        // optional
  "effective_model": "fast-quant-v2",
  "cost_estimate_tokens": "~1.2k",
  "cost_estimate_usd": "$0.012",
  "quota_risk": "medium",
  "quota_assumptions": "95p traffic, batch=8, cache_hit=20%",
  "fallback_reason": "quota"
}
```
Sam (Telemetry): We'll emit events with that payload (redact sensitive fields). Can we also log the model routing decision ID for correlation?
Priya (BE): Yes, routing decision id (route_decision_id) is cheap to attach. It helps debug.
Ava (PM): Ok next: rollout UX. When we do canary rollouts of new models, saved views that pinned an older model might break. Do we auto-rewrite pins to compatible variants? Or surface a migration flow?
Nina (Design): Prefer explicit migration. Show a post-save banner "We detected compatible variants for pinned model — migrate now / remind me later". Avoid silently changing pinned models.
Diego (FE): We'll need endpoints: /saved_views/:id/suggested_migrations which returns suggested_migration: [{from:fast-quant, to:fast-quant-v2, reason:"latency"}]. UI can render a one-click migration.
Priya (BE): Backend: generate suggestions via model-catalog relationships. Also check compatibility matrix (tokenizer, output shapes). Not all models are safe to auto-migrate.
Sam (Telemetry): Track migration accept/decline events. Useful for metric: % pinned views migrated after rollout.
Ava (PM): Security/enterprise concerns: private deployments may have models not present in hosted catalog — suggestion flow should be disabled for private.
Priya (BE): We'll gate suggestions by org_capabilities: model_catalog_sync flagged. If false, return empty suggestions.
Diego (FE): One more implementation nit: saved views are cached heavily. Need cache invalidation when model catalog updates or routing policy changes — otherwise UI will show stale effective_model.
Priya (BE): We'll add a small TTL (5m) and push invalidation events on catalog updates. Also include cache_version in the preview response.
Nina (Design): Sounds good. UX checklist for engineering:
- show pinned vs effective model
- quota risk pill with hover assumptions
- migration banner for suggested variants
- CTA to re-evaluate under different routing policies
Ava (PM): Action items:
- Priya: add fields to saved view preview API + route_decision_id + cache_version (ETA 3d)
- Sam: add telemetry events + fallback_reason enums (ETA 2d)
- Diego: FE mocks + implement preview panel changes + honor cache_version (ETA 1wk)
- Nina: finalize microcopy and pill colors (ETA 2d)
Priya (BE): I'll open a PR with API changes and include a migration compatibility flag.
Diego (FE): I'll attach a quick prototype gif in this thread when I have the preview panel working.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered for infra/preview — build 2026.4 is rolling to staging :rocket:
Ava (PM): Thanks all. We'll check back in the weekly product sync. If anyone spots edge cases (multi-model routes, region routing), drop them here and we'll triage. :thumbsup:
